notes: Matched on 105 of 121 A units and 115 B units (the committee and college texts share wording, each coded on its own). Main disagreements: (1) unit_stance on disclosure and verification units (A require vs B neutral or permit), resolved to require where the source says must or should document/declare/attribute, neutral for pure verification duties and for suggested discussion topics in the Graduate School page; (2) phase and actor on principles and institutional statements (general vs during-work/before-course, all vs admin vs student), resolved by whether the sentence is a principle (general), a statement by the committee/Board (admin), or addressed to instructors (instructor); (3) policy_type: opacity of AI and 'attribution is not a valid source for facts' made UNCOVERED rather than stretched into P31/P30; footnote about ChatGPT use set to P84 not P48; P18 for AI-generated prose; P59 for TA teaching use; (4) modality: source word controls ('should' not must; 'reminder' and 'limitation' sentences informs; 'not a substitute' must-not); (5) normalized policy: B wrote policies where A anchored a truncated span, so B's policy was used when the anchor lacked a condition (e.g. 'if properly documented'), and a merged B unit was split in two (verify vs document the steps; delete-if-unlocatable; usage form vs attestation). Two college-text pairs the matcher shifted by one sentence were re-paired by hand. 16 A-only units (premise, definition, compliance, contact, sanction clauses, split-off rules) and 10 B-only units (privacy reasons, ownership restatements, simulation documentation, grad-school nuance) were checked against the source; all were real and kept. Stance matched on all three documents (delegates). new_types empty on both sides.
